note: Group names for register families: one name per policy that several items share, describing the issue across jurisdictions. The menu shows each family as one expandable row (DECISIONS E-99). Each item keeps its own assessment.

families.title: Restrictive planning and zoning in every state and territory
families.summary: Each jurisdiction's planning system limits what can be built where, and each is assessed as strongly negative. New South Wales has started to loosen some rules (employment zones, transport-oriented development).

families.title: Insurance duty still charged in most states and territories
families.summary: Most states and territories tax insurance premiums. The ACT abolished its duty in 2016, and Victoria is phasing out the duty on business insurance from 2024.

families.title: Work health and safety laws harmonised everywhere except Victoria
families.summary: The model laws were adopted between 2012 and 2022, Western Australia last. Victoria keeps its own occupational health and safety law, so employers in several states still meet two sets of rules.

families.title: Automatic recognition of occupational licences, without Queensland
families.summary: Most jurisdictions began recognising each other's occupational licences automatically in 2021 and 2022. Queensland stays out, so workers moving to or from it still apply for a separate licence.

families.title: Stamp duty on home purchases in every state except the ACT's phase-out
families.summary: Seven states and territories tax property purchases, each assessed as strongly negative. The ACT is phasing out its duty in favour of general rates.

families.title: One national registration scheme for health practitioners (2010)
families.summary: Every state and territory joined the national scheme in 2010 (Western Australia in October), so one registration covers the whole country.

families.title: Inconsistent adoption of the 2022 building code standards
families.summary: States adopted the 2022 energy and accessibility standards at different times, from October 2023 to May 2025, and several varied them, so builders working across borders meet different requirements.

families.title: NDIS provider regulation moved to one national commission (2018 to 2020)
families.summary: The NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission took over regulating disability providers state by state, from New South Wales and South Australia in 2018 to Western Australia in 2020.

families.title: Occupational licensing that differs state by state
families.summary: Each state and territory licenses trades such as electrical, plumbing and building work under its own laws, with different requirements and scope.

families.title: Payroll tax: eight separate state and territory regimes
families.summary: Each state and territory sets its own payroll tax threshold, rates, exemptions and administration, so employers in several jurisdictions deal with several regimes.

families.title: Pharmacist treatment of urinary tract infections, introduced state by state (2020 to 2024)
families.summary: Each state and territory let pharmacists treat uncomplicated urinary tract infections on its own timetable, from Queensland in 2020 to the Northern Territory in 2024.

families.title: Ride-sharing legalised state by state (2015 to 2019)
families.summary: Each state and territory legalised ride-sharing and reformed taxi rules separately, from the ACT in 2015 to Western Australia in 2019.

families.title: Separate container deposit schemes in each state
families.summary: Each scheme was set up separately, between 2012 and 2025 for those listed, with its own coordinator and fees. Environment ministers agreed in 2021 to harmonise eligible containers, refunds and labelling.

families.title: One national heavy vehicle law, without Western Australia and the Northern Territory
families.summary: Six jurisdictions adopted the Heavy Vehicle National Law in 2014. Western Australia and the Northern Territory did not, so operators crossing northern Australia work under separate systems.

families.title: Shop trading hours deregulated piecemeal, state by state
families.summary: States have extended trading hours in separate steps, such as Sunday or Boxing Day trading, so the hours shops may open still differ between states.

families.title: Mandatory fuel price reporting, introduced state by state (2016 to 2025)
families.summary: Each state and territory set up its own real-time fuel price reporting scheme, from New South Wales in 2016 to Victoria in 2025.

families.title: National energy retail rules, adopted state by state and with variations
families.summary: Five jurisdictions adopted the national framework between 2012 and 2015. The Harper review found it had yet to be applied without major derogations in Victoria and Queensland.

families.title: Mandatory industry codes of conduct
families.summary: Commonwealth codes that govern dealings between businesses in dairy, horticulture, sugar, groceries and franchising.

families.title: Electronic conveyancing made mandatory, state by state (2018 to 2023)
families.summary: States required property transfers to be lodged electronically on different dates, from New South Wales in 2018 to Queensland in 2023.

families.title: Pharmacy ownership limited to pharmacists, with different limits in each state
families.summary: States limit pharmacy ownership to pharmacists and cap how many pharmacies one pharmacist may own; the caps differ from state to state.

families.title: Where pharmacies may open and who may own them
families.summary: Commonwealth location rules decide where new pharmacies may open, alongside Queensland's ownership regime and changes to dispensing.

families.title: Retail energy prices deregulated state by state (2009 to 2016)
families.summary: States removed retail energy price regulation separately, from Victoria in 2009 to south-east Queensland in 2016.

families.title: Lockout and last-drinks laws: Sydney's introduced and repealed, Queensland's trading cap
families.summary: Sydney's 2014 lockout laws were repealed in 2020 and 2021. Queensland applied a statewide 2am trading cap from 2016.

families.title: Contestable training funding, introduced state by state (2009 to 2015)
families.summary: States opened government training funding to private providers separately, from Victoria in 2009 to New South Wales in 2015.

families.title: Stamp duty on commercial property being phased out in some states
families.summary: The ACT, South Australia and Victoria are each removing stamp duty on commercial property, in different ways and on different timetables.

families.title: Compulsory third-party insurance schemes redesigned state by state
families.summary: New South Wales, South Australia and the ACT each redesigned their motor accident insurance schemes in a different way, with different roles for private insurers.

families.title: Fair Work changes 2022 to 2024
families.summary: Commonwealth workplace law changes: multi-employer bargaining, same job same pay orders for labour hire, and the right to disconnect.

families.title: Uniform legal profession law in three states only
families.summary: New South Wales and Victoria (2015) and Western Australia (2022) regulate lawyers under one uniform law; the other states and territories keep their own laws.

families.title: One national rail safety law, reached in stages (2013 to 2024)
families.summary: The national rail safety law and regulator began in 2013; Victoria moved to direct national regulation in 2019 and Western Australia applied the full law in 2024.

families.title: Short-term rental rules that differ by state
families.summary: New South Wales, Victoria and Western Australia each regulate short-term rentals differently: a code, register and night cap, a levy, or a register.

families.title: Ports leased to private operators, state by state
families.summary: Queensland, the Northern Territory and Victoria leased their main ports to private operators on long leases, with different terms.

families.title: Card surcharging rules
families.summary: Limits on card surcharges since 2016, and their removal for eftpos, Mastercard and Visa from October 2026.

families.title: Harper competition law reforms (2017)
families.summary: The 2017 changes to the Competition and Consumer Act: the effects test for misuse of market power and the concerted practices prohibition.

families.title: Default electricity price caps (2019)
families.summary: Default offers that cap standing electricity prices, set nationally for some regions and separately in Victoria.

families.title: Insolvency and restructuring reforms
families.summary: The safe harbour for directors attempting a turnaround (2017) and simplified restructuring for small businesses (2021).

families.title: Non-compete clauses and the proposed ban
families.summary: Non-compete clauses are common in employment contracts; a ban for workers below a pay threshold is proposed from 2027.

families.title: One national quality framework for childcare (2012)
families.summary: The National Quality Framework began in 2012, in Western Australia from August of that year.

families.title: R&D Tax Incentive
families.summary: The R&D Tax Incentive replaced the R&D tax concession in 2011 and was redesigned in 2021.

families.title: Unfair contract terms protections for small business
families.summary: Protections extended to small business contracts in 2016, then made illegal with penalties in 2023.

families.title: New building practitioner registration schemes in New South Wales and Victoria (2021)
families.summary: Both states began registering building designers or engineers in 2021, under different schemes.

families.title: Small-bar licences in New South Wales and Western Australia
families.summary: Cheaper licences for small bars, introduced in Western Australia in 2007 and New South Wales in 2013.

families.title: Next-day fuel price caps in Victoria and the Northern Territory (2026)
families.summary: Both jurisdictions began requiring retailers to commit to next-day fuel prices in 2026, under different designs.

families.title: Limits on new liquor licences: a moratorium in the Northern Territory, a freeze lifted in Victoria
families.summary: The Northern Territory stopped new takeaway liquor licences in 2017; Victoria lifted its freeze on new late-night licences in 2023.

families.title: Taxi and booked-hire licensing reforms
families.summary: Queensland's booked-hire licences (2017) and South Australia's removal of its metropolitan taxi licence cap (2025).

families.title: Full retail contestability for electricity (Queensland and Tasmania)
families.summary: Households were allowed to choose their electricity retailer, in Queensland from 2007 and Tasmania from 2014.

families.title: Gaming machine monopolies ended in Victoria and Tasmania
families.summary: Victoria ended the gaming machine duopoly in 2012 and Tasmania the Federal Group monopoly in 2023.
